previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, transfusion-dependent anemia likely due to myelodysplastic syndrome, and recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin was admitted for acute-on-chronic left shoulder pain and dyspnea on lying flat. Imaging confirmed pulmonary edema consistent with heart failure exacerbation, and she was treated with IV furosemide and supplemental oxygen, which was successfully weaned. Her shoulder pain, attributed to severe osteoarthritis, improved with acetaminophen, a lidocaine patch, and PRN oxycodone. Hypokalemia on admission was corrected with IV and oral supplementation. Asymptomatic bacteriuria was noted, but antibiotics were withheld due to lack of symptoms, and the Foley catheter was removed on hospital day two. She was discharged home with home health services, stable vital signs, improved symptoms, and clear instructions to monitor weight and follow up with her providers.
